name: PepsiCo
description: PepsiCo is a snack, cereal and beverage company, and its profits come mostly from food, not cola. PepsiCo Foods North America (Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Quaker) is 29 percent of revenue but 46 percent of segment operating profit. Beverages in North America (Pepsi, Mountain Dew, Gatorade) are sold by PepsiCo's own bottling and distribution network, while outside North America it often sells concentrate to independent bottlers. International food and snack businesses (EMEA, Latin America, Asia Pacific) are together 47 percent of revenue. Net revenue was $93.9B in 2025 (+2%) but operating profit fell 11 percent after a Rockstar energy-brand impairment and higher commodity and tariff costs.

businessLines.name: PepsiCo Foods North America (PFNA)
businessLines.how: Snacks made in PepsiCo plants and sold to independent distributors and retailers, with a large direct delivery network stocking shelves; revenue is volume times price, margin is the highest in the company (22.4%).
businessLines.description: All convenient food businesses in the US and Canada: Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Fritos, Ruffles, Tostitos, Quaker, Pearl Milling Company, Sabra.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses

businessLines.name: PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA)
businessLines.how: Makes concentrate and fountain syrup and also runs its own bottling plants and distribution, selling finished drinks to retailers and independent distributors; capital-heavy and much lower margin (3.9% in 2025) than snacks. 2025 profit includes $1,523M of impairment and other charges (Rockstar brand) and $422M of acquisition-related charges (poppi).
businessLines.description: Pepsi, Mountain Dew, Gatorade, Aquafina, Bubly, Propel and others in the US and Canada.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses

businessLines.marketShare: 16% of the US liquid refreshment beverage category by estimated retail sales in 2025 (company-wide beverages); Coca-Cola 20%

businessLines.name: International Beverages Franchise (IB Franchise)
businessLines.how: Sells beverage concentrate to authorized and independent bottlers who make, sell and distribute the drink; asset-light royalty-style economics (35.4% margin); SodaStream sells sparkling-water makers and flavours.
businessLines.description: International franchise beverage business (7UP, Aquafina, Gatorade, Mirinda, Mountain Dew, Pepsi, Sting) and SodaStream; Lipton tea through a joint venture with Unilever.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses

businessLines.name: Europe (EMEA)
businessLines.how: Mix of manufactured snacks and owned beverage operations sold to retailers; Russia revenue was $4,768M in 2025 vs $3,880M in 2024.
businessLines.description: Food, snack and beverage businesses in the EMEA segment.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses

businessLines.name: Latin America Foods
businessLines.how: Snacks made and sold to stores directly and through distributors; Brazil revenue $1,782M.
businessLines.description: Convenient food business in Latin America (brands not itemised in the extract read).

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses

businessLines.name: Asia Pacific Foods
businessLines.how: Snacks and foods sold through distributors and retail; low margin (8.0%).
businessLines.description: Convenient food businesses in Asia Pacific.

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating profit after the charges noted in the 10-K segment table; excludes $2,018M of corporate unallocated expenses
